fields.headline: Marine engineering software development, by naval architects
fields.lead: Lasan Marine Co., Ltd. builds custom software for naval architecture and marine engineering teams: calculation tools for stability, hydrostatics, resistance and structure; Rhino/Grasshopper plugins, AutoCAD and Maxsurf automation; web apps for shipyards and design offices; and AI agents for technical documents. We design vessels ourselves, so a naval architect reviews every tool before you see it.

fields.heading: Problems we solve for engineering teams
fields.intro: Most requests start with a task an engineer repeats on every project. These are the ones we hear most often.

items.problem: Loading conditions are run one by one in Maxsurf
items.context: Every change to lightship, tanks or cargo means re-running loadcases by hand and copying the results into the stability booklet.
items.solution: A script that drives Maxsurf through its automation interface, runs the loadcase batch and writes the results straight into your report template.

items.problem: The same modelling steps repeat on every hull
items.context: Frames, longitudinals, plate expansions or hull variants are rebuilt manually in Rhino each time a parameter changes.
items.solution: Grasshopper components or a RhinoCommon plugin that generates the geometry from your own design rules and parameters.

items.problem: Critical calculations live in spreadsheets nobody wants to touch
items.context: Hydrostatics, criteria checks or scantlings sit in workbooks with hidden formulas, no tests and one person who understands them.
items.solution: A tested calculation tool with the same method made explicit, which also generates the calculation document from the same inputs.

items.problem: Estimates, materials and drawing revisions are spread across files
items.context: Quotes are rebuilt from scratch, the BOM lives in Excel and nobody is sure which drawing revision the reviewer commented on.
items.solution: A web app for estimating, material take-off and drawing and document control, with access for your team and, if you wish, your clients.

items.problem: Engineers spend hours on rule look-ups and routine documents
items.context: Finding the right clause, drafting standard reports and pulling data out of specifications takes time that should go into design.
items.solution: AI agents that search the rules and standards you provide, draft routine documents and extract technical data, with an engineer checking the output.

fields.heading: Why hire naval architects who write code

items.title: Domain review on every deliverable
items.desc: Formulas, units, sign conventions, criteria and edge cases are checked by a naval architect, not only by a test suite.

items.title: No translation layer
items.desc: You discuss GZ curves, loadcases and frame spacing directly with the people who write the code, so requirements do not get lost between a project manager and a developer.

items.title: Tools we use in our own design work
items.desc: Our calculation tools are built for and tested in our own ship-design projects. Several are public and free, so you can judge the work before you contact us.

fields.heading: In-house tools you can open today

items.name: Ship stability simulator
items.desc: Problem: checking transverse stability quickly at the concept stage. What it does: computes the GZ curve, GM and angle of vanishing stability in the browser, checks basic IS Code 2008 criteria and exports a report to Word and Excel.

items.name: Resistance and power simulator
items.desc: Problem: estimating installed power for planing craft and small passenger vessels. What it does: Savitsky and Holtrop–Mennen predictions of effective and brake power across the speed range.

items.name: 3D steel structure simulator
items.desc: Problem: explaining how a steel hull is built up. What it does: an interactive 3D model of parts, panels, sections and blocks, with a walk-through inside the hull, the assembly sequence and graded exercises (Vietnamese interface).

items.name: Shaft, engine and power tools
items.desc: Problem: quick checks during machinery selection. What they do: a preliminary propeller-shaft diameter check, a searchable marine-engine database and a kW/HP/PS converter.

items.name: Ship design brief app
items.desc: Problem: incomplete requirements at the start of a design. What it does: a structured brief that saves drafts in the browser and exports a clean document to share or print.

fields.heading: How a project runs
fields.intro: The same five stages apply to a small Grasshopper component and to a full web application; only their length changes.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.desc: A call about the task, the users and the software involved. We sign an NDA before you share drawings, models or internal methods.

steps.title: Specification
steps.desc: A written spec: inputs, outputs, methods, reference cases and acceptance tests, with a fixed-scope quote or a time-and-materials estimate.

steps.title: Iterations
steps.desc: Working builds in short cycles, so your engineers test on real projects early and adjust the requirements before they are expensive to change.

steps.title: Validation
steps.desc: Results compared with your reference tools, hand calculations or test data and with the agreed test cases. Any differences are explained and documented.

steps.title: Handover
steps.desc: Source code, build and deployment instructions, documentation and training, followed by maintenance if you want it.

fields.heading: Engagement models, IP and time zone
fields.content:
Three ways to work with us

  • Fixed scope. For a well-defined tool or plugin. We agree the specification and price before work starts; changes are handled through written change requests, so there are no surprises on the invoice.
  • Time and materials. For work where the requirements will evolve, such as automating an existing workflow step by step. You pay for the time spent and receive regular progress reports.
  • Dedicated developer. A developer working on your backlog, in your repository and communication channels, with naval-architect review available when the work needs it.

Your IP stays yours

Source code, models and documentation written for your project belong to you, as set out in the contract. We sign an NDA before you share any details. Your drawings, models and data are used only for your project, are shared only with the people working on it, and are returned or deleted at the end if you ask.

Working across time zones

We are in Nha Trang, Vietnam (UTC+7) and work in English by email, chat and video call. Our afternoon overlaps the European morning, our morning overlaps the afternoon in Australia and New Zealand, and Japan and Korea are only two hours ahead, so we share most of the working day.

fields.heading: What you receive at handover
fields.body: Deliverables are agreed in the specification. Depending on the project, they include:

items.text: Full source code, delivered to your repository
Test cases and the validation record
Training for the engineers who will use it

items.title: Who owns the source code and the IP?
items.content: You do. Source code, models and documentation written for your project belong to you, and this is stated in the contract. The code is delivered to your repository, not held back on our side.

items.title: Will you sign an NDA before we share details?
items.content: Yes. We sign your NDA, or provide ours, before you send drawings, models, rules or internal calculation methods. Your data is used only for your project and returned or deleted at the end if you ask.

items.title: Which CAD and engineering platforms do you work with?
items.content: Rhino and Grasshopper (RhinoCommon plugins in C#, Grasshopper components and scripts), AutoCAD, Maxsurf through its automation interface, Excel, and web applications. If your software exposes an API or a scripting interface we can usually work with it. Tell us the product and version and we will confirm before quoting.

items.title: How do you validate engineering results?
items.content: Reference cases are agreed in the specification: results from the tools you already trust, hand calculations, published examples or test data. Every release is checked against them and a naval architect reviews the method and the results. Differences are explained in a validation record you keep.

items.title: Can you take over our existing spreadsheets, macros or code?
items.content: Yes. We often start from an existing workbook or script, document what it actually calculates, add tests and then rebuild or extend it. Your current results become the first reference cases.

items.title: Do you provide maintenance after handover?
items.content: Yes, if you want it. We can fix issues, update the software for new versions of the host CAD platform and add features under a maintenance arrangement or as new fixed-scope work. Because you hold the source code, you can also maintain it in-house.

items.title: How do we start?
items.content: Email hello@lasanmarine.com with a short description of the task and the software involved. We arrange a call, sign an NDA, look at sample files and send a proposal with the scope and the engagement model that fits.

fields.heading: Have a task your engineers repeat on every project?
fields.description: Send a short description, the software you use and a sample file if you can share one. We will tell you how we would approach it and which engagement model fits.
